titulo: Painel de entrega — tickets herdados da Enaakshi

pedido: a) Base só com o basic é aceitável?
d) Joiners/leavers/licença: base cheia ou proporcional?
e) Tirar o transporte da base?
Aasim: base mensal ou salário de janeiro?
itens.texto:
Hi @abagwan, @srai,

Under the Yemen Social Insurance Law No. 26 of 1991 (as amended by Law 16/2008), published by GCSS:

a) Basic-only is not acceptable. The contribution wage (Art. 2) is basic salary plus allowances; GCSS specifies "allowances of a permanent and stable nature" and excludes only overtime, grants and incentive bonuses. The January point is correct: Art. 14(1) — contributions are calculated on the wages received in January of each year, even if wages rise or fall during the year. So the base is the January wage (basic + fixed allowances such as housing and transport), locked January–December and reset each January.

d) Joiners after January: base = full wage of the joining month until the next January (Art. 14(2)) — no proration. Leavers: no contribution is due for the month in which service ends, regardless of days worked (Art. 15(2)). Unpaid absence deductions do not reduce the base (Art. 15(1)); during formal unpaid leave contributions are suspended unless the employee elects, in writing to GCSS, to pay both shares (Art. 50(3)).

e) No — transport, as a fixed monthly allowance, stays in the base.

On your question: the law requires the January-based annual base, not a monthly recalculation. Our YE-CCG-001 / YE-WTC-001 will be aligned accordingly.

Source: GCSS — Law 26/1991 Arts. 2, 14, 15, 50 (https://gcss-yemen.org/قانون-اللتأمينات/) and "Mandatory insurance" page (https://gcss-yemen.org/التأمين-الإلزامي-لصاحب-العمل/).
afirm: Base = salário + allowances permanentes e estáveis; fora OT, gratificações e bônus
Base = salário de janeiro de cada ano (art. 14(1))
Joiner: salário do mês de admissão até o próximo janeiro (art. 14(2))
Leaver: sem contribuição no mês de saída (art. 15(2))
Faltas não reduzem a base (art. 15(1)); licença sem vencimento suspende salvo opção (art. 50(3))
Decorre do item 3 da página GCSS
alem: "Our YE-CCG-001 / YE-WTC-001 will be aligned accordingly": correção de artefato, ninguém pediu
pend: Arts. 14(2), 15 e 50 só pelo agente (PDF digitalizado): reler antes de gravar

pedido: A OT entra na base do SS?
OT com data de fev/mar paga em abril: como fica?
itens.texto:
@srai @abagwan

Federal Iraq: overtime is part of the social security base. Law No. 18 of 2023 defines the wage as "all monetary and in-kind payments and allowances of all kinds received by the insured person in return for their work" (Art. 1, Eleventh), and contributions are calculated on the total wages and allowances received (Art. 14, Second; Art. 15, First), capped at 5x the minimum wage (IQD 1,750,000/month). Labour Law No. 37 of 2015, Art. 1(14), also includes overtime pay in the wage. The current exclusion of overtime (WT 62110–62139) from the Federal SS base will be corrected in the CCG, WTC and configuration.

Kurdistan Region: overtime remains excluded. Law No. 39 of 1971 limits the wage to the fixed wage paid permanently (Art. 1), and contributions are based on the January wage of the year (Art. 26(b)).

[Overtime for February/March paid in April: <decisão pendente: contributed in the month it is paid (April), within that month's ceiling / recalculated in February/March>.]

Please confirm whether REF-03-147 and REF-03-148 are registered under Federal Iraq or the Kurdistan Region.
afirm: Salário = pagamentos e allowances de todo tipo (Lei 18/2023 art. 1, Eleventh)
Contribuição sobre o total de salários e allowances (art. 15, First)
Labour Law 37/2015 art. 1(14) inclui OT no salário
KRI: Lei 39/1971 arts. 1 e 26(b), OT fora

pedido: Gross Salary inclui o Exempt Income Amount?
itens.texto: @lli Yes, Gross Salary should include the Exempt Income Amount. In the spec, Taxable Income (Base) = Gross − Exempt Income Amount − Employee SS − Social Unity Fund − Personal Exemption, so Gross must be the total employment income paid in the month (taxable + exempt), which is also what Art. 60 of Income Tax Law 7/2010 requires the employer to list ("income received"); the Art. 55 items (e.g. end-of-service indemnity, leave payout) are employment income on which the tax does not apply. Field explanations (Gross Salary, Exempt Income Amount) and the Sample File formula updated accordingly (v1.1).

pedido: Teto de 15% é do básico anual?
Lógica do básico anual em 5 cenários
itens.texto:
Hi Mohit,

Confirmed: the cap is 15% of the employee's ANNUAL basic salary, not year-to-date basic.

- Income Tax Regulations, 2016 (L.I. 2244), reg. 5(2): "if the total of the bonus payments made by that employer to the employee during the year of assessment does not exceed fifteen percent of the annual basic salary of that employee, withhold tax ... at the rate of five percent", and the excess is added to employment income and taxed under the First Schedule.
- Reg. 5(6): "calculate the tax on the basic salary of the employee for the year of assessment to which the bonus relates."
- GRA Practice Note DT/2016/011, s. 4.11.2, examples 1-2: a bonus paid in July is tested against the full annual basic (e.g. 15% x 100,000), not against basic paid to date.

The law does not give a formula for joiners, leavers or salary changes. Proposed logic (re-estimated each period, as reg. 4(3) allows for PAYE estimates):

Annual basic (AB) = basic actually paid in the tax year to date (incl. current period, prorated where applicable, and basic arrears/adjustments for that year) + current contractual monthly basic x remaining months of employment in the year.
Cap = 15% x AB. Bonus at 5% this period = MIN(cumulative bonus YTD; Cap) - amount already taxed at 5% in prior periods. The rest of the bonus goes to PAYE.

1. Salary change: 10,000 Jan-Mar, 12,000 from Apr, bonus in Apr: AB = 30,000 + 12,000 + 12,000 x 8 = 138,000; cap 20,700 (YTD basic would give 6,300).
2. Mid-year joiner (joins 1 Jul, 10,000): AB = 6 x 10,000 = 60,000; cap 9,000. The basis period for a joiner runs from the start date to 31 Dec (Practice Note s. 4.1(c)). Bonuses from a previous employer do not count ("made by that employer").
3. Mid-month joiner (joins 16 Jul, July prorated 5,000): AB = 5,000 + 5 x 10,000 = 55,000; cap 8,250.
4. Mid-year leaver (leaves 30 Sep): remaining months stop at the leaving date: AB = 9 x 10,000 = 90,000; cap 13,500.
5. Mid-month leaver (leaves 15 Sep, Sept prorated 5,000): AB = 8 x 10,000 + 5,000 = 85,000; cap 12,750.

True-up: in the December or final (termination) period, AB = actual basic paid in the year; recompute the 5% portion against the final cap and post the difference (2572 adjustment, with the amount moved into or out of PAYE). Example: bonus 18,000 paid in March against an estimated cap of 18,000, employee leaves 30 Sep, final cap 13,500: 2572 -225 and +4,500 to taxable income in the final period.

Two points to confirm with the client:
- "Current monthly basic x 12" overstates AB for joiners, leavers and mid-year increases. Under the logic above, case 2 in the workbook gives Other Tax 1,716.80 / PAYE 26,785.97, not 1,800.00 / 26,286.78 (case 1 is unchanged: 1,000.00 / 7,086.78).
- Per reg. 5(6), if the March bonus relates to performance year 2025, the cap uses the 2025 basic salary, not 2026.

Kind regards,
afirm: Exemplo GRA: bônus de julho × básico anual cheio
Período base do joiner até 31/12 (Practice Note s. 4.1(c))
Contas dos 5 cenários e do true-up
alem: Bloco 'Two points to confirm with the client' (workbook e ano do bônus): útil, mas não perguntado

pedido: Revisar a configuração (tax, SSS, PhilHealth, HDMF, 13º, 2316)
Se errado: flags e impacto nos reports
itens.texto:
Hi @kpham,

**Income tax / BIR 2316** — Both elements are exempt from income tax and withholding tax on compensation:
- SSS maternity benefit: NIRC Sec. 32(B)(6)(e) ("Benefits received from or enjoyed under the Social Security System") and RR 2-98 Sec. 2.78.1(B)(1)(e).
- Employer-paid salary differential (RA 11210 Sec. 5(c)): BIR RMC No. 105-2019 (3 Sep 2019) classifies the differential as a benefit under the SSS law and concludes it "is exempt from income and withholding taxes".

In the PH WTC, 79406 (Maternity Leave) and 79452 (SSS Salary Differential) are already set to Subject to Tax = No (Non-MWE and MWE) and excluded from Period Taxable Income (58552). Both map to BIR 2316 item 37, "Salaries and Other Forms of Compensation", under Non-Taxable/Exempt Compensation (Form 2316, Sept 2021 ENCS). Neither falls in the ₱90,000 13th-month/other-benefits bucket (item 34) or in de minimis (item 35). The tax and 2316 configuration matches the client's reference.

**PhilHealth** — The premium is computed on the Monthly Basic Salary, "the fixed basic rate of an employee", which excludes allowances and is not reduced by "leave(s) without pay, absences, or other similar circumstances" (PhilHealth Circular 2020-0005 Rev. 1, Sec. IV.F and V.B). Sec. V.D adds: "the premium contribution of women who are on maternity leave shall be regularly remitted to PhilHealth". The SSS maternity benefit and the salary differential are therefore not part of the PhilHealth base. The premium for the leave months remains due on the employee's full contractual Monthly Basic Salary. The WTC currently has Subject to PhilHealth = Yes on both 79406 and 79452.

**SSS** — SSS contributions are based on "compensation", defined as "all actual remuneration for employment" (RA 11199 Sec. 8(f)). The SSS maternity benefit is an SSS benefit that the employer advances and the SSS reimburses (RA 11199 Sec. 14-A; RA 11210 IRR Rule VI Sec. 4), so it is not remuneration for employment. For the salary differential, we found no SSS issuance on its inclusion in the Monthly Salary Credit. The RA 11210 IRR (Rule III Sec. 2) defines the female worker's "full pay" as the SSS maternity benefit plus the salary differential, and BIR RMC 105-2019 treats the differential as part of the SSS maternity benefit. The WTC currently has Subject to SSS = Yes on both.

**HDMF (Pag-IBIG)** — The contribution base is "basic monthly salary plus mandated cost of living allowance" (RA 9679 Sec. 4(b)). Pag-IBIG Circular No. 460 defines Fund Salary as remuneration payable by the employer "for work done… or for services rendered", capped at ₱10,000. The SSS maternity benefit is not remuneration paid by the employer. For the salary differential, we found no HDMF issuance addressing it. The WTC currently has Subject to HDMF = Yes on both.

**13th month pay** — The salary differential is included as part of basic salary for the 13th-month computation (DOLE-BWC Handbook on Workers' Statutory Monetary Benefits 2023, Ch. 13 item H, citing DOLE Department Advisory No. 01 s. 2019).

**SIT / parallel run** — Tax, 1601-C and 2316 results are not affected. In any SIT/parallel-run period where 79406 or 79452 was paid, those amounts were included in the SSS (58551), PhilHealth (58554) and HDMF (58521) bases.

Kind regards,
afirm: PhilHealth: base = MBS, não reduzida por licença (PC 2020-0005)
⚠️ PDF digitalizado, lido só pelo agente
HDMF: base = salário básico + COLA (RA 9679; Circ. 460)
não vimos os outputs do SIT
alem: Texto longo (532 palavras); o pedido tem 5 itens, então parte se justifica
pend: Reler PhilHealth, SSS e HDMF na fonte

itens.texto:
@rgupta Confirming the Submission ID for records 3101, 4101 and 5000. Source: eIndkomst: Teknisk vejledning v11.6 (info.skat.dk, oid=1745538), §§ 3.2, 3.4, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8.

1. **IndberetningsID** (3101 pos 13-28, 4101 pos 12-27, 5000 pos 13-28; alphanumeric, max 16) is a **new ID we generate for every occurrence of the record**. It must never have been used before for the same SE-nr. and must not repeat across 3101, 4101 and 5000, or on two 5000 records in the same file. It is neither the SE number nor the Hoved_indberetningsID of record 1000. § 3.2: "Den der indberetter skal angive unikke indberetningsID-er i record 3101, 4101 og 5000."
2. **Record 4101** therefore has two IDs: field 3 IndberetningsID = a new ID for the reversal itself; field 4 ReferenceID = the IndberetningsID of the **original record 5000 (or 3101)** being reversed. It cannot be the main submission ID: "Der kan ikke tilbageføres på hovedindberetningsID/fil niveau" (§ 3.2). A full reversal of a period needs one 4101 per original IndberetningsID ("I praksis en record 4101 pr. indberetningsident").
3. **ReferenceID in 3101 and 5000** (pos 29-44) is optional. If filled, it must be the earlier IndberetningsID of the record being changed ("Den tidligere indberetningsident skal bruges her"), not the main submission ID. Otherwise leave it blank.
4. Record 3101 is not linked to the correction marker. It is sent for a zero return (field 8 = "N", field 9 = 0000) or for fields 0059/0400 (§ 4.6).

For development, this means the IndberetningsIDs of every submitted 3101/5000 need to be stored per SE-nr. and period, so that the 4101 can reference them. Spec rows 54, 55, 64, 65, 72 and 73 will be updated in v3.6 accordingly.
